mentions.author: hackermailman
mentions.story: Ask HN: How do you remember things without tests?
mentions.text:
As noted in other comments, if you build something as you learn the material you'll remember it. My learning strategy is usually:

Think up idea
No idea how to implement it
Look at university lecture notes for background material
Read lecture notes, read assigned text
Implement idea while I read the text and notes
Notice my implementation is poorly inefficient
Read more advanced notes/papers to optimize
Rewrite idea, success!

This is exactly what I did when I read Modern Compiler Implementation in ML by Andrew Appel. This was the course I used [course] though it was an earlier version. Afterwards I collected a lot of compiler optimization notes, like here [course]
